requirements.requirement: Configure node1 so the running kernel boots with audit=1.
requirements.summary: A real reboot changed the boot ID, after which /proc/cmdline contained audit=1 and auditctl reported the kernel audit subsystem as enabled. The node recovered to system state running with no failed units.

Before reboot, grubby and the BLS entries showed audit=1 on every normal and rescue boot entry. Following the acknowledged reboot and changed boot identity, the live command line and all saved entries still contained audit=1.

overall_summary: The task is fully satisfied. Direct observations establish a healthy pre-reboot baseline, acknowledged reboot disruption, a changed boot identity, recovery, audit=1 on the running kernel, and persistent audit=1 configuration in all saved boot entries. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong for this single-node task: boot identity, restart acknowledgement, system recovery, failed-unit state, and service sockets were observed coherently.
limitations: No application data or cluster-specific state was explicitly checked during the restart protocol; none was identified in the single-node task contract or managed topology.
auditd was inactive after reboot, although this does not contradict the requested kernel parameter: auditctl directly reported enabled 1.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The grubby update was the required persistent configuration change (cmd-7010a6d91bdc407d), and the scheduled reboot was necessary to prove boot-time activation and persistence (cmd-40b9747a593b4523). Other commands were read-only verification or bounded observations during the reboot. Afterward, the node had no failed services, package health remained good, and listening services matched the baseline apart from expected post-reboot process IDs. The temporary-file differences were ordinary regenerated systemd private directories associated with the new boot.
